course_description:
Fundamental descriptions of flow; viscous internal and external flows; turbomachinery; fundamentals of compressible flow; compressible pipe flows; flow measurement.

An understanding of the underlying physics and mathematical description of fluid mechanics is necessary to analyse systems that have a fluid as the working medium.ﾠ Mechanical engineers have to deal with fluid mechanics in applications ranging from heating and ventilation systems, transport of fluids in piping systems, fluids in physiological systems,ﾠ through to transport applications such as cars, ships, aircraft and spacecraft. ﾠThe design of fluid machinery such as pumps, compressors and turbines requires the ability to analyse fluid flows.ﾠ This course builds on material in MECH2410: Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics and applies it to viscous internal and external flows, both laminar and turbulent, compressible flows and turbomachinery. Whilst fluid flows must satisfy the well-established basic laws of mechanics, the analysis can become very complex and experimental results must often be used to model practical flows. Therefore, the importance of making measurements in fluid flows is also stressed in this course. Some methods and techniques used to make measurements in fluid flows are addressed together with an assessment of their uncertainty.

You should plan to spend at least 10 hours per week on this course in order to obtain a passing grade.

course_aims: This courseﾠextends your knowledge of fluid mechanics to include the description and analysis of multi-dimensional, viscous and compressible flows. At the completion of the course you should be able to apply your understanding of fluid mechanics to a wide range of important engineering systems ranging from pipe flow in the process industries to flow of air around aircraft. The applied class exercises are used to develop problem solving skills while the laboratory work aims to develop practical skills in flow measurement, analysis and interpretation of results.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand and apply advanced fluid mechanics concepts
Analyse systems involving laminar, transitional and turbulent internal flow
Analyse external flow problems involving boundary layers, transition to turbulence, flow separation, pressure, skin friction and induced drag, and finite span aerofoils
Analyse compressible flow problems involving isentropic flow, nozzle flows, normal and oblique shock waves, compressible frictional flows and compressible flow with heat transfer
Understand fluid mechanics experiments and work as a team to analyse, interpret and report on experimental data

assessment_details.title: Experiment 1 (Aerofoil)
assessment_details.due_date: Group report submission is due at 2pm, exactly one week after completion of practical.
assessment_details.task_description: All students to attend on-campus laboratories in assigned groups. Participation in the on-campus laboratory is required to receive a grade for the report. If you cannot attend the laboratory due to medical grounds/exceptional circumstances, you will need to apply for an extension. Students with an approved extension for laboratory attendance will be rescheduled in an available laboratory session. Students with approved extensions beyond the final available laboratory will attend a virtual make-up lab in week 7. Complete all preparation work in your individual Laboratory Logbook and familiarise yourself with the experimental procedure. Pre-work will be checked by the demonstrator during the laboratory. Record all measurements and observations in your individual Laboratory Logbook. Remember: everything goes into your Logbook. In teams of 4-5 students (the group you did the lab with), prepare a brief (not formal) laboratory report. Use the practical instructions as a guide. The report should focus on the analysis and discussion of the results. As a guideline the submitted reports should contain the following parts and information : A brief introduction on the goals of the experiment A clear description of methods and techniques used to process and analyse the experimental data (including quantification of experimental uncertainty); All processed data from experiment; all raw data from the experiment (in an appendix) Discussion of results, including: discussion of the main results of the experiment Discuss any discrepancies between experiment and theory Answers to questions (where appropriate) The Laboratory Instructions available from Blackboard include additional instructions. The tasks should be completed in a logbook or alternate well-organised system. For any disputes, you will be required to produce this logbook/system as evidence to support your case. Please refer to Blackboard for a detailed marking criteria. If, for whatever reason, you find that your group is not functioning effectively, please contact your Course Coordinator for support. Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 7 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
When submitting an extension request, you must specify whether you are seeking an extension on the pre-work + laboratory participation component, and/or the report component.
Students with an approved extension for laboratory attendance will be rescheduled in an available laboratory session. Students with approved extensions beyond the final available laboratory will attend a virtual make-up lab in week 7. Please contact the Course Coordinator with evidence of your approved extension to facilitate this.
Extensions on the group report are limited to 7 days as feedback is provided to students following 14 calendar days from the latest possible due date.
For the group report component, your request will need to include a document demonstrating group agreement from at least 50% of the members of the group. If your request is for the pre-work + laboratory participation component, a blank document will suffice.
Note: you cannot use a discretionary extension request for this task.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
The late penalty applies for the report submission only.
No late submission is possible for the pre-work, as it must be completed by beginning of practical.

assessment_details.title: Experiment 2 and 3 logbook entries
assessment_details.task_description: All students attend Laboratories 2 and 3 on-campus in your timetabled group. Participation in the on-campus laboratory is required to receive a grade for the corresponding logbook entry. If you cannot attend the laboratory due to medical grounds/exceptional circumstances, you will need to apply for an extension. Students with an approved extension for laboratory attendance will be rescheduled in an available laboratory session. Students with approved extensions beyond the final available laboratory will have the logbook entry for the laboratory they attended scaled up to 14%. Students who did not attend either Laboratory 2 and 3 with appropriate approved extensions will be given an alternative assessment due at 29/10/2026 at 2:00 pm. For each laboratory: Complete all preparation work in your individual Laboratory Logbook (or log-file) and bring this to your lab sessions. This will be checked at the start of the laboratory ( Pre-work ). Study course material relevant to practical (e.g. by reading relevant chapters in course textbook and reviewing lecture material). Read and understand the experimental instructions. It is your responsibility to be familiar with the appropriate analysis methods. In teams of typically 4-5 students, record all measurements and observations in one Laboratory Logbook (or log-file). As a team continue to complete the required analysis and jointly write a short conclusion (1/4 page) about the experiment. The team analysis and conclusion will be marked after the laboratory. ( Execution ) The Laboratory Instructions available from Blackboard include additional instructions. The tasks should be completed in a logbook or alternate well-organised system.
